subject: Export-control friendly subprocessor roster & escrow plan — action required
messages:
From: Sudeep Rao <sudeep.r@advancedmedica.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 09:13:00 +0000
Subject: Export-control friendly subprocessor roster & escrow plan — request

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing our compliance packet for an upcoming export-control review and need a few items from Redwood to close the loop on our end:

1) A current, machine-readable subprocessor roster (CSV preferred) that includes country of operation, residency of data-at-rest, and whether the subprocessor holds an export-control or dual-use licensure (if applicable).
2) A short description of any escrow arrangements or custody plans for critical ML artifacts (model weights, fine-tuning checkpoints) and whether those arrangements have residency or export constraints.

Our auditors have asked that the roster explicitly flag any processors that could trigger additional export-review (e.g., vendors operating from restricted jurisdictions). If possible, can you provide both the roster and a 1-page escrow summary by end of week?

Thank you — this is time-sensitive for their intake window.

Regards,
Sudeep Rao
Advanced Medica 
Head of Procurement
procurement@advancedmedica.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sudeep Rao <sudeep.r@advancedmedica.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 12:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Export-control friendly subprocessor roster & escrow plan — request

Hi Sudeep — thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. We're on it.

Quick notes on scope so we deliver exactly what you need:
- We'll produce a CSV with columns: vendor_name, service_description, country_operational, data_residency, export_risk_flag (low/medium/high), contract_reference, SOC2_scope (yes/no), onshore_status (yes/no).
- For escrow: we'll provide a one-page summary describing our standard escrow partners (where applicable), what artifacts are placed into escrow, access conditions, and any residency restrictions. Redwood uses third-party escrow for certain enterprise customers; where we don't, we describe key custody controls and KMS residency.

Irene, can you confirm whether the latest roster includes the export_risk_flag column and share the current CSV snapshot? Logan — can you draft the 1-page escrow summary and call out any providers that store artifacts outside the EU?

Sudeep — we'll aim to get the CSV + escrow summary to you by EOD Friday (2025-04-25). If your auditors need an interim note sooner, say the export-sensitive rows only, let me know.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0104

Hi team — attaching the current roster snapshot and a short changelog.

Summary (high level):
- The CSV now includes export_risk_flag (calculated based on country + vendor export controls) and data_residency as separate fields.
- We flagged 6 vendors as medium/high due to operating in jurisdictions with additional review requirements; those rows include a brief comment column that explains the trigger.
- SOC2_scope is populated for vendors that touch tokens or telemetry; others are no.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20250422.csv (see key columns), roster_changelog_20250422.txt

Notes for Logan: the escrow summary should call out that for model artifacts we generally use on-prem key-wrapping + customer-managed keys when needed; only enterprise contracts include third-party escrow. Where escrow exists, several partners store copies in the US and UK — please flag any non-EU storage.

Irene

Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sudeep Rao <sudeep.r@advancedmedica.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 24 Apr 2025 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Export-control friendly subprocessor roster & escrow plan — request

Hi Sudeep — attaching the one-page escrow summary per Tessa's notes. Key points:

- Escrow coverage: Redwood offers a standard escrow option for enterprise customers that includes model artifacts and a metadata index; otherwise custody is via customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
- Providers: When escrow is used, providers we engage store redundancy in the US and UK; we maintain contractual controls to ensure access is governed by disclosure conditions and MFA.
- Residency: For customers requiring EU-only residency, we can negotiate onshore storage or omit third-party escrow and instead provide a signed custody attest plus KMS key-handling documentation.

I've also included a short spreadsheet extract with the three vendors we currently classify as medium/high export risk and the justification.

Files attached: escrow_arrangement_summary_20250422.pdf, redwood_subprocessor_roster_20250422.csv

Let me know if you need any additional level of detail for the auditors — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the package through.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Lead, Vendor Risk
Redwood Inference
